# Sovrium agent options

> Generated from the Sovrium schema by scripts/build/generate-skill-references.ts — do not edit. It carries no version on purpose: when it and the binary you run disagree, the binary is right.

Every option of the app's own AI agents, and of the AI access a table or an automation grants, with the command that prints its full entry from the binary you run. Providers, models and speech-to-text are environment variables: `sovrium docs configuration/env-vars-ai`.

- [`agents[]`](#agents)

## `agents[]`

| Option | Kind | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sovrium docs config agents[]` | object | Complete AI agent configuration including identity, model parameters, approval workflows, tool access, limits, permissions, and scheduling. |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].name` | string | Unique kebab-case identifier for this agent |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].description` | string | What this agent is for, in one line (up to 2,000 characters, no line break). The operator console draws it under the agent name, and the admin agents list carries it on the agent item. Display text only: the agent never reads it, so it is not a prompt; write instructions in `systemPrompt`. |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].role` | string | Auth role this agent operates as (must exist in auth.roles) |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].model` | string | LLM model override for this agent (defaults to AI_MODEL env var) |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].temperature` | number | Temperature override for LLM responses (0-1 inclusive) |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].maxTokens` | number | Maximum output tokens override (positive integer) |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].systemPrompt` | string | System prompt defining agent personality and behavioral rules |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].instructions` | array | Additional behavioral instructions appended as numbered rules to the system prompt |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].instructions[]` | string | A single behavioral instruction |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].enabled` | boolean | Whether agent can execute (defaults to true) |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].approval` | object | Human-in-the-loop approval workflow configuration for agent actions. Controls which actions need human review before execution. |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].approval.mode` | enum | Approval mode: none (no approval), all (every action), selective (specific actions only) |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].approval.required` | array | Actions requiring approval (must be a subset of capabilities.actions). Required when mode=selective. |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].approval.required[]` | string | Action type requiring approval |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].approval.timeout` | number | Seconds before a pending approval expires unexecuted |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].approval.escalation` | object | Escalation configuration for pending approval requests. |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].approval.escalation.after` | number | Seconds before escalation triggers (must be less than timeout) |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].approval.escalation.to` | string | Role to escalate to (must reference a role defined in auth.roles) |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].tools` | object | Tool allowlist defining which tables and actions an agent can access. Implements double-gate security (RBAC + allowlist). |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].tools.tables` | array | Table names the agent can access (must reference tables defined in the schema) |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].tools.tables[]` | string | Table name the agent can access |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].tools.actions` | array | Action types the agent can perform |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].tools.actions[]` | enum | Action type the agent can perform (type.operator format) |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].tools.browser` | object | The hosts and stored sessions an agent granted `browser.use` may reach. Required with `browser.use`, refused without it. |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].tools.browser.allowedHosts` | array | Every host the browser may reach for this agent. A start address on another host is refused, and a request any page makes to another host is blocked, whatever a page tells the agent. |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].tools.browser.allowedHosts[]` | string | A host name, optionally with a port: "app.example.com", "*.example.com" (any sub-domain, not the domain itself), "login.example.com:8443". Written out, never a template. |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].tools.browser.sessions` | array | Stored browser sessions the agent may start from — the sign-ins a `browser/run` keeps. The agent never receives a password: a session is how it reaches pages behind a sign-in. Any other session name is refused. |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].tools.browser.sessions[]` | string | Name of a stored browser session the agent may use |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].limits` | object | Rate limits, token budgets, and concurrency caps for an agent. All fields default to system values when omitted. |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].limits.maxActionsPerMinute` | number | Maximum DB/email actions per minute |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].limits.maxTokensPerDay` | number | Maximum LLM tokens consumed per 24h period, reset at midnight UTC |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].limits.maxConcurrentTasks` | number | Maximum simultaneous task executions |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].memory` | object | Memory configuration for an AI agent: knowledge retrieval and learned facts |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].memory.knowledge` | object | RAG-based semantic retrieval from the configured knowledge sources. Vectors are stored by the active database — a pgvector column on PostgreSQL, a packed float blob on SQLite. |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].memory.knowledge.enabled` | boolean | Whether knowledge memory is enabled |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].memory.knowledge.sources` | array | Knowledge source names to search (must reference configured knowledge bases) |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].memory.knowledge.sources[]` | string | Knowledge source name |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].memory.knowledge.retrievalLimit` | number | Maximum number of documents to retrieve per query |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].memory.knowledge.similarityThreshold` | number | Minimum similarity score (0-1) a retrieved document must reach |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].memory.facts` | object | Persistent AI-managed key-value facts learned across sessions, retrieved by semantic relevance |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].memory.facts.enabled` | boolean | Whether facts memory is enabled |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].memory.facts.maxFacts` | number | Maximum number of facts the agent can store |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].memory.facts.namespace` | string | Namespace that isolates this agent's facts from every other agent's |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].permissions` | object | RBAC integration model for AI agents. Agents are stored as auth.user records with type=agent and inherit role-based permissions. |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].permissions.type` | enum | User type discriminator — always 'agent' for AI agents |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].permissions.trigger` | enum \| array | Who can trigger this agent. 'all', 'authenticated', or role array ['admin', 'member']. |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].permissions.trigger[]` | string | One role name that has access — a built-in role or one declared in `auth.roles`. |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].schedule` | object | Runs the agent on a recurring schedule, written as a cron expression in a named time zone. |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].schedule.cron` | string | Standard 5-field cron expression |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].schedule.timezone` | string | IANA timezone identifier (defaults to the operator timezone, SOVRIUM_TIMEZONE, UTC when unset) |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].schedule.taskPrompt` | string | Prompt sent to the LLM as the user message for each scheduled execution |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].knowledge` | object | Knowledge configuration defining what data sources to embed for RAG-based retrieval. |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].knowledge.tables` | array | Table data sources for knowledge embedding |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].knowledge.tables[]` | object | Table data source configuration for agent knowledge embedding |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].knowledge.tables[].table` | string | Table name to embed for knowledge retrieval |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].knowledge.tables[].fields` | array | Fields to embed from this table |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].knowledge.tables[].fields[]` | string | Field name to include in embedding |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].knowledge.tables[].filter` | object | Key-value filter conditions for knowledge table rows |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].knowledge.documents` | array | Document file sources for knowledge embedding |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].knowledge.documents[]` | object | Document file data source for agent knowledge embedding |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].knowledge.documents[].path` | string | Path to the document file for knowledge embedding |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].knowledge.documents[].label` | string | Human-readable label for the knowledge document |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].mcp` | object | Which external MCP servers the agent may reach, and which of their tools it is offered |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].mcp.servers` | array | The external MCP servers this agent may reach, by the names the operator declared in MCP_CLIENT_SERVERS. An agent that names none is offered no external tool. A name the environment does not declare stops the boot. |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].mcp.servers[]` | string | The name of an external MCP server declared by the operator in MCP_CLIENT_SERVERS (lowercase kebab-case). |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].mcp.allowedTools` | array | Narrows the tools of the servers in mcp.servers to these names: a tool's own name (lookup_company) or its qualified <server>__<tool> form. Every tool of those servers when omitted. |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].mcp.allowedTools[]` | string | One tool to keep: the tool's own name (lookup_company) or its qualified <server>__<tool> form. |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].skills` | array | The skill directories this agent may use. Each holds a SKILL.md whose frontmatter declares a name and a description. A listed directory whose SKILL.md is missing, or whose frontmatter lacks a name or a description, stops the boot with a message naming the file, and makes `sovrium validate` exit 1 with the same message. |
| `sovrium docs config agents[].skills[]` | string | A skill directory holding a SKILL.md, written relative to the directory that holds the config with '/' (e.g. 'skills/quote-review'). It must stay inside the project: no leading '/', no '..' segment, no backslash. |

## `tables[].aiAccess`

| Option | Kind | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess` | boolean \| object | Per-entity declaration of MCP/AI exposure intent. Boolean shorthand (true = enabled with defaults) or rich config object. Schema author declares; operator activates via MCP_ENABLED env var. |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.description` | string | Hand-written description shown to the AI client. Overrides auto-generated descriptions. The single biggest UX lever for steering AI behavior — explain when to use this tool, what context the AI needs, and any non-obvious constraints. |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.operations` | array | Subset of CRUD operations to expose. Defaults to all 5 (read, list, create, update, delete) for tables. Automations and actions ignore this field — they expose a single invocation tool. |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.operations[]` | enum | One CRUD operation to expose as a tool — `read` and `list` are the two reads, `create`, `update` and `delete` the three writes. |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.fieldExposure` | enum | Field exposure mode. Defaults to permissioned (only fields the connecting role can read/write per RBAC). |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.whitelistFields` | array | Fields to expose when fieldExposure=whitelist. Required and must be non-empty when fieldExposure=whitelist; ignored otherwise. |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.whitelistFields[]` | string | One field name to expose, spelled as the table declares it. |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.annotations` | object | Risk hints exposed to MCP clients to drive auto-approve vs. confirmation UX. Optional; sensible defaults are derived from the operation type when unset. |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.annotations.readOnly` | boolean | Marks the table's tools as read-only for MCP clients (readOnlyHint), which may then run them without asking. Applies only when every exposed operation is read or list; on a table that also exposes create, update or delete, read tools are always read-only and write tools never are, whatever this says. |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.annotations.destructive` | boolean | Tool performs destructive operations (delete, send email, charge card); clients should require explicit confirmation. Maps to MCP destructiveHint. |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.annotations.idempotent` | boolean | Calling the tool twice with the same args is safe (no duplicate side effects). Maps to MCP idempotentHint. |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.annotations.openWorld` | boolean | Tool reaches outside the local app (external API, network call). Maps to MCP openWorldHint. |
| `sovrium docs config tables[].aiAccess.requireConfirmation` | boolean | Force destructiveHint=true on the resulting MCP tool regardless of operation type. Use for automations/actions whose effects are non-reversible (e.g. sending emails) even if technically idempotent. |
